```{r}
#' DataTrans: A Package for Engineering Data Transformation and Analysis
#'
#' @description
#' The DataTrans package provides specialized tools for engineering data
#' preprocessing, transformation, and analysis. Originally developed for
#' turbine performance data, it offers general-purpose data transformation
#' functions applicable to various engineering and scientific datasets.
#'
#' @section Main Functions:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item \code{\link{load_turbine_data}}: Load and prepare turbine dataset
#'   \item \code{\link{normalize_data}}: Normalize numerical variables
#'   \item \code{\link{clean_engineering_data}}: Clean engineering datasets
#'   \item \code{\link{detect_outliers}}: Detect statistical outliers
#'   \item \code{\link{analyze_correlations}}: Analyze variable correlations
#'   \item \code{\link{plot_turbine_performance}}: Visualize turbine performance
#' }
#'
#' @docType package
#' @name DataTrans
#' @keywords internal
"_PACKAGE"

# Package environment for storing settings
.datatrans_env <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())

#' @import dplyr
#' @import ggplot2
#' @importFrom tibble as_tibble
#' @importFrom stats sd median cor
#' @importFrom tidyr drop_na pivot_longer
```

```{r}
#' Load Turbine Thrust Dataset
#'
#' @description
#' Loads the turbine thrust dataset included with the package or from a file.
#' This dataset contains turbine performance measurements with thrust (y) as
#' the response variable and six predictor variables (x1-x6).
#'
#' @param filepath Optional path to Excel or CSV file. If NULL, uses built-in data.
#' @param use_builtin Logical. If TRUE, uses built-in dataset (default).
#'
#' @return A tibble containing the turbine data with columns:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item y: Thrust output (response variable)
#'   \item x1-x6: Predictor variables
#' }
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' # Use built-in data
#' data <- load_turbine_data()
#' 
#' # Load from file
#' data <- load_turbine_data("turbine_thrust.xlsx")
#' }
#'
#' @export
load_turbine_data <- function(filepath = NULL, use_builtin = TRUE) {
  if (use_builtin || is.null(filepath)) {
    # Create built-in dataset from provided data
    turbine_data <- tibble::tibble(
      y = c(4540, 4315, 4095, 3650, 3200, 4833, 4617, 4340, 3820, 3368,
            4445, 4188, 3981, 3622, 3125, 4560, 4340, 4115, 3630, 3210,
            4330, 4119, 3891, 3467, 3045, 4411, 4203, 3968, 3531, 3074,
            4350, 4128, 3940, 3480, 3064, 4402, 4180, 3973, 3530, 3080),
      x1 = c(2140, 2016, 1905, 1675, 1474, 2239, 2120, 1990, 1702, 1487,
             2107, 1973, 1864, 1674, 1440, 2165, 2048, 1916, 1658, 1489,
             2062, 1929, 1815, 1595, 1400, 2047, 1935, 1807, 1591, 1388,
             2071, 1944, 1831, 1612, 1410, 2066, 1954, 1835, 1616, 1407),
      x2 = c(20640, 20280, 19860, 18980, 18100, 20740, 20305, 19961, 18916, 18012,
             20520, 20130, 19780, 19020, 18030, 20680, 20340, 19860, 18950, 18700,
             20500, 20050, 19680, 18890, 17870, 20540, 20160, 19750, 18890, 17870,
             20460, 20010, 19640, 18710, 17780, 20520, 20150, 19750, 18850, 17910),
      x3 = c(30250, 30010, 29780, 29330, 28960, 30083, 29831, 29604, 29088, 28675,
             30120, 29920, 29720, 29370, 28940, 30160, 29960, 29710, 29250, 28890,
             30190, 29960, 29770, 29360, 28960, 30160, 29940, 29760, 29350, 28910,
             30180, 29940, 29750, 29360, 28900, 30170, 29950, 29740, 29320, 28910),
      x4 = c(205, 195, 184, 164, 144, 216, 206, 196, 171, 149,
             195, 190, 180, 161, 139, 208, 199, 187, 164, 145,
             193, 183, 173, 153, 134, 193, 184, 173, 153, 133,
             198, 186, 178, 156, 136, 197, 188, 178, 156, 137),
      x5 = c(1732, 1697, 1662, 1598, 1541, 1709, 1669, 1640, 1572, 1522,
             1740, 1711, 1682, 1630, 1572, 1704, 1679, 1642, 1576, 1528,
             1748, 1713, 1684, 1624, 1569, 1746, 1714, 1679, 1621, 1561,
             1729, 1692, 1667, 1609, 1552, 1758, 1729, 1690, 1616, 1569),
      x6 = c(99, 100, 97, 97, 97, 87, 87, 87, 85, 85,
             101, 100, 100, 100, 101, 98, 96, 94, 94, 94,
             101, 100, 100, 99, 100, 99, 99, 99, 99, 99,
             102, 101, 101, 101, 101, 100, 99, 99, 99, 100)
    )
    
    # Store in package environment
    .datatrans_env$turbine_data <- turbine_data
    return(turbine_data)
    
  } else {
    # Load from file
    if (grepl("\\.xlsx?$", filepath, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      if (!requireNamespace("readxl", quietly = TRUE)) {
        stop("Package 'readxl' is required to read Excel files")
      }
      data <- readxl::read_excel(filepath)
    } else if (grepl("\\.csv$", filepath, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      data <- utils::read.csv(filepath)
    } else {
      stop("Unsupported file format. Please use .xlsx, .xls, or .csv")
    }
    
    return(tibble::as_tibble(data))
  }
}
```

```{r}
#' Normalize Numerical Variables
#'
#' @description
#' Standardizes numerical variables using z-score normalization or min-max scaling.
#' Particularly useful for engineering datasets where variables have different scales.
#'
#' @param data A data frame or tibble containing the data to normalize
#' @param method Character string specifying the normalization method.
#'   Options: "zscore" (default) or "minmax"
#' @param exclude Character vector of column names to exclude from normalization
#' @param verbose Logical indicating whether to print progress messages
#'
#' @return A tibble with normalized numerical columns
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{
#' data <- load_turbine_data()
#' normalized <- normalize_data(data, method = "zscore")
#' }
#'
#' @export
normalize_data <- function(data, method = c("zscore", "minmax"), 
                          exclude = NULL, verbose = TRUE) {
  
  # Input validation
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    stop("Input must be a data frame or tibble")
  }
  
  method <- match.arg(method)
  
  # Convert to tibble if not already
  data <- tibble::as_tibble(data)
  
  # Identify numerical columns
  num_cols <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.numeric)]
  
  # Remove excluded columns
  if (!is.null(exclude)) {
    num_cols <- setdiff(num_cols, exclude)
  }
  
  if (length(num_cols) == 0) {
    if (verbose) warning("No numerical columns found to normalize")
    return(data)
  }
  
  if (verbose) {
    message(sprintf("DataTrans: Normalizing %d columns using %s method", 
                   length(num_cols), method))
    message(sprintf("Columns: %s", paste(num_cols, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  
  # Apply normalization
  result <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(num_cols),
      ~ {
        if (method == "zscore") {
          # Z-score normalization
          if (sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) == 0) {
            warning("Standard deviation is zero for a column. Returning original values.")
            return(.x)
          }
          (.x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
        } else {
          # Min-max normalization
          min_val <- min(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
          max_val <- max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
          if (max_val == min_val) {
            warning("Min and max are equal for a column. Returning original values.")
            return(.x)
          }
          (.x - min_val) / (max_val - min_val)
        }
      },
      .names = "{.col}_norm"
    ))
  
  if (verbose) {
    message("DataTrans: Normalization completed successfully")
    
    # Show summary of normalized columns
    norm_summary <- result %>%
      dplyr::select(dplyr::ends_with("_norm")) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), 
                                    list(mean = mean, sd = sd), 
                                    na.rm = TRUE))
    
    if (method == "zscore") {
      message("Z-score normalization check:")
      message("  Expected means ≈ 0, standard deviations ≈ 1")
    } else {
      message("Min-max normalization check:")
      message("  Expected ranges: 0 to 1")
    }
  }
  
  return(result)
}
```

```{r}
#' Clean Engineering Dataset
#'
#' @description
#' Performs comprehensive cleaning of engineering datasets including:
#' - Removing duplicate rows
#' - Handling missing values
#' - Removing constant columns
#' - Basic outlier filtering (optional)
#'
#' @param data A data frame or tibble
#' @param remove_duplicates Logical, remove duplicate rows (default: TRUE)
#' @param handle_missing Method for handling missing values: 
#'   "remove", "mean", "median", or "knn" (default: "remove")
#' @param remove_constant Logical, remove columns with zero variance (default: TRUE)
#' @param outlier_threshold Z-score threshold for outlier removal (default: 3.5, set to NULL to skip)
#' @param verbose Logical, print progress messages (default: TRUE)
#'
#' @return A cleaned tibble
#'
#' @export
clean_engineering_data <- function(data, 
                                   remove_duplicates = TRUE,
                                   handle_missing = c("remove", "mean", "median", "knn"),
                                   remove_constant = TRUE,
                                   outlier_threshold = 3.5,
                                   verbose = TRUE) {
  
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    stop("Input must be a data frame or tibble")
  }
  
  handle_missing <- match.arg(handle_missing)
  original_rows <- nrow(data)
  original_cols <- ncol(data)
  
  if (verbose) {
    message("DataTrans: Starting data cleaning process")
    message(sprintf("  Original dimensions: %d rows × %d columns", 
                   original_rows, original_cols))
  }
  
  # Convert to tibble
  data <- tibble::as_tibble(data)
  
  # 1. Remove duplicates
  if (remove_duplicates) {
    data <- dplyr::distinct(data)
    if (verbose) {
      duplicates_removed <- original_rows - nrow(data)
      if (duplicates_removed > 0) {
        message(sprintf("  Removed %d duplicate rows", duplicates_removed))
      }
    }
  }
  
  # 2. Handle missing values
  na_count <- sum(is.na(data))
  if (na_count > 0) {
    if (verbose) {
      message(sprintf("  Found %d missing values", na_count))
    }
    
    if (handle_missing == "remove") {
      data <- tidyr::drop_na(data)
      if (verbose) {
        message("  Removed rows with missing values")
      }
    } else {
      # Impute missing values
      num_cols <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.numeric)]
      
      for (col in num_cols) {
        na_idx <- is.na(data[[col]])
        
        if (any(na_idx)) {
          if (handle_missing == "mean") {
            imp_val <- mean(data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
          } else if (handle_missing == "median") {
            imp_val <- median(data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
          } else if (handle_missing == "knn") {
            # Simple mean imputation (for simplicity)
            # In production, use proper KNN imputation
            imp_val <- mean(data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
          }
          
          data[[col]][na_idx] <- imp_val
        }
      }
      
      if (verbose) {
        message(sprintf("  Imputed missing values using %s method", handle_missing))
      }
    }
  }
  
  # 3. Remove constant columns
  if (remove_constant) {
    constant_cols <- sapply(data, function(x) {
      if (is.numeric(x)) {
        var(x, na.rm = TRUE) == 0
      } else {
        FALSE
      }
    })
    
    if (any(constant_cols)) {
      data <- data[, !constant_cols]
      if (verbose) {
        message(sprintf("  Removed %d constant columns", sum(constant_cols)))
      }
    }
  }
  
  # 4. Remove extreme outliers (optional)
  if (!is.null(outlier_threshold)) {
    num_cols <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.numeric)]
    outlier_rows <- integer(0)
    
    for (col in num_cols) {
      z_scores <- abs(scale(data[[col]]))
      outlier_rows <- union(outlier_rows, which(z_scores > outlier_threshold))
    }
    
    if (length(outlier_rows) > 0) {
      data <- data[-outlier_rows, ]
      if (verbose) {
        message(sprintf("  Removed %d rows with extreme outliers", length(outlier_rows)))
      }
    }
  }
  
  if (verbose) {
    message(sprintf("  Final dimensions: %d rows × %d columns", 
                   nrow(data), ncol(data)))
    message("DataTrans: Data cleaning completed")
  }
  
  return(data)
}
```

```{r}
#' Analyze Variable Correlations
#'
#' @description
#' Computes and visualizes correlations between variables in a dataset.
#' Particularly useful for identifying relationships in engineering data.
#'
#' @param data A data frame or tibble
#' @param target_var Optional target variable for computing correlations
#' @param method Correlation method: "pearson" (default), "spearman", or "kendall"
#' @param plot Logical, whether to create a correlation heatmap (default: TRUE)
#' @param threshold Minimum absolute correlation to highlight (default: 0.7)
#'
#' @return A list containing:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item correlation_matrix: Full correlation matrix
#'   \item target_correlations: Correlations with target variable (if provided)
#'   \item strong_correlations: Pairs with |correlation| > threshold
#' }
#'
#' @export
analyze_correlations <- function(data, target_var = NULL, 
                                 method = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall"),
                                 plot = TRUE, threshold = 0.7) {
  
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    stop("Input must be a data frame or tibble")
  }
  
  method <- match.arg(method)
  
  # Select only numerical columns
  num_data <- data[, sapply(data, is.numeric)]
  
  if (ncol(num_data) < 2) {
    stop("Need at least 2 numerical columns for correlation analysis")
  }
  
  # Compute correlation matrix
  cor_matrix <- cor(num_data, use = "complete.obs", method = method)
  
  # Find strong correlations
  strong_pairs <- which(abs(cor_matrix) > threshold & 
                         upper.tri(cor_matrix), arr.ind = TRUE)
  
  strong_correlations <- data.frame(
    Variable1 = rownames(cor_matrix)[strong_pairs[, 1]],
    Variable2 = colnames(cor_matrix)[strong_pairs[, 2]],
    Correlation = cor_matrix[strong_pairs]
  )
  
  # Sort by absolute correlation
  strong_correlations <- strong_correlations[
    order(abs(strong_correlations$Correlation), decreasing = TRUE),
  ]
  
  # Target variable correlations
  target_cor <- NULL
  if (!is.null(target_var)) {
    if (target_var %in% colnames(num_data)) {
      target_cor <- cor_matrix[, target_var, drop = FALSE]
      target_cor <- target_cor[rownames(target_cor) != target_var, , drop = FALSE]
      colnames(target_cor) <- "Correlation"
      target_cor <- target_cor[order(abs(target_cor), decreasing = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
    } else {
      warning(sprintf("Target variable '%s' not found in numerical columns", target_var))
    }
  }
  
  # Create plot if requested
  if (plot && requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
    # Prepare data for heatmap
    cor_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_matrix))
    names(cor_df) <- c("Var1", "Var2", "Correlation")
    
    # Remove diagonal and lower triangle
    cor_df <- cor_df[cor_df$Var1 != cor_df$Var2, ]
    cor_df <- cor_df[order(cor_df$Var1, cor_df$Var2), ]
    
    # Create heatmap
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(cor_df, ggplot2::aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = Correlation)) +
      ggplot2::geom_tile(color = "white") +
      ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", high = "red", mid = "white", 
                                   midpoint = 0, limit = c(-1, 1)) +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
      ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
      ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Correlation Matrix",
        x = "",
        y = "",
        fill = "Correlation"
      ) +
      ggplot2::coord_fixed()
    
    print(p)
  }
  
  # Return results
  result <- list(
    correlation_matrix = cor_matrix,
    target_correlations = target_cor,
    strong_correlations = strong_correlations,
    method = method
  )
  
  return(result)
}
```

```{r}
#' Plot Turbine Performance Relationships
#'
#' @description
#' Creates visualization plots for turbine performance analysis.
#' Shows relationships between thrust (y) and predictor variables.
#'
#' @param data Turbine dataset (from load_turbine_data())
#' @param x_var Predictor variable to plot against thrust (default: "x1")
#' @param plot_type Type of plot: "scatter" (default), "histogram", or "boxplot"
#' @param add_regression Logical, add regression line to scatter plot (default: TRUE)
#' @param color_by Optional variable for color coding points
#'
#' @return A ggplot object
#'
#' @export
plot_turbine_performance <- function(data, 
                                     x_var = "x1",
                                     plot_type = c("scatter", "histogram", "boxplot"),
                                     add_regression = TRUE,
                                     color_by = NULL) {
  
  plot_type <- match.arg(plot_type)
  
  if (!x_var %in% names(data)) {
    stop(sprintf("Variable '%s' not found in dataset", x_var))
  }
  
  if (!"y" %in% names(data)) {
    stop("Response variable 'y' not found in dataset")
  }
  
  # Create plot based on type
  if (plot_type == "scatter") {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(x = .data[[x_var]], y = y))
    
    if (!is.null(color_by) && color_by %in% names(data)) {
      p <- p + ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(color = .data[[color_by]]), 
                                   alpha = 0.7, size = 2)
    } else {
      p <- p + ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2, color = "steelblue")
    }
    
    if (add_regression) {
      p <- p + ggplot2::geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, 
                                    color = "darkred", alpha = 0.2)
    }
    
    p <- p + ggplot2::labs(
      title = sprintf("Turbine Thrust vs %s", x_var),
      x = x_var,
      y = "Thrust (y)",
      color = if (!is.null(color_by)) color_by else NULL
    )
    
  } else if (plot_type == "histogram") {
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(x = y)) +
      ggplot2::geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7, color = "white") +
      ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Distribution of Turbine Thrust",
        x = "Thrust (y)",
        y = "Frequency"
      )
    
  } else if (plot_type == "boxplot") {
    # Create categorical version of x_var for boxplot
    if (is.numeric(data[[x_var]])) {
      data[[paste0(x_var, "_cat")]] <- cut(data[[x_var]], breaks = 5)
      x_var_plot <- paste0(x_var, "_cat")
    } else {
      x_var_plot <- x_var
    }
    
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(x = .data[[x_var_plot]], y = y)) +
      ggplot2::geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
      ggplot2::geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
      ggplot2::labs(
        title = sprintf("Thrust Distribution by %s", x_var),
        x = x_var,
        y = "Thrust (y)"
      ) +
      ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  }
  
  p <- p + ggplot2::theme_minimal()
  
  return(p)
}
```

```{r}
#' Summarize Dataset Statistics
#'
#' @description
#' Provides comprehensive statistical summary of a dataset.
#' Includes counts, means, standard deviations, and missing values.
#'
#' @param data A data frame or tibble
#' @param detailed Logical, include detailed percentiles (default: FALSE)
#'
#' @return A list containing summary statistics
#'
#' @export
summarize_dataset <- function(data, detailed = FALSE) {
  
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    stop("Input must be a data frame or tibble")
  }
  
  # Basic information
  basic_info <- list(
    n_rows = nrow(data),
    n_cols = ncol(data),
    n_numeric = sum(sapply(data, is.numeric)),
    n_factor = sum(sapply(data, is.factor)),
    n_character = sum(sapply(data, is.character)),
    n_logical = sum(sapply(data, is.logical)),
    total_missing = sum(is.na(data))
  )
  
  # Summary for numeric columns
  num_cols <- names(data)[sapply(data, is.numeric)]
  numeric_summary <- list()
  
  if (length(num_cols) > 0) {
    numeric_summary <- lapply(num_cols, function(col) {
      col_data <- data[[col]]
      stats <- list(
        mean = mean(col_data, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd = sd(col_data, na.rm = TRUE),
        min = min(col_data, na.rm = TRUE),
        max = max(col_data, na.rm = TRUE),
        median = median(col_data, na.rm = TRUE),
        missing = sum(is.na(col_data)),
        missing_pct = sum(is.na(col_data)) / length(col_data) * 100
      )
      
      if (detailed) {
        stats$q1 <- quantile(col_data, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
        stats$q3 <- quantile(col_data, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
        stats$iqr <- stats$q3 - stats$q1
        stats$skewness <- moments::skewness(col_data, na.rm = TRUE)
        stats$kurtosis <- moments::kurtosis(col_data, na.rm = TRUE)
      }
      
      return(stats)
    })
    
    names(numeric_summary) <- num_cols
  }
  
  # Summary for categorical columns
  cat_cols <- names(data)[sapply(data, function(x) is.factor(x) | is.character(x))]
  categorical_summary <- list()
  
  if (length(cat_cols) > 0) {
    categorical_summary <- lapply(cat_cols, function(col) {
      col_data <- data[[col]]
      list(
        n_unique = length(unique(col_data)),
        top_categories = names(sort(table(col_data), decreasing = TRUE))[1:3],
        missing = sum(is.na(col_data)),
        missing_pct = sum(is.na(col_data)) / length(col_data) * 100
      )
    })
    
    names(categorical_summary) <- cat_cols
  }
  
  # Return comprehensive summary
  result <- list(
    basic_info = basic_info,
    numeric_summary = numeric_summary,
    categorical_summary = categorical_summary,
    column_names = names(data),
    data_types = sapply(data, class)
  )
  
  class(result) <- "DataTransSummary"
  return(result)
}

#' Print method for DataTransSummary
#'
#' @param x DataTransSummary object
#' @param ... Additional arguments
#'
#' @export
print.DataTransSummary <- function(x, ...) {
  cat("=== DataTrans Dataset Summary ===\n\n")
  
  cat("Basic Information:\n")
  cat(sprintf("  Rows: %d\n", x$basic_info$n_rows))
  cat(sprintf("  Columns: %d\n", x$basic_info$n_cols))
  cat(sprintf("  Numeric columns: %d\n", x$basic_info$n_numeric))
  cat(sprintf("  Categorical columns: %d\n", x$basic_info$n_factor + x$basic_info$n_character))
  cat(sprintf("  Total missing values: %d\n", x$basic_info$total_missing))
  
  if (length(x$numeric_summary) > 0) {
    cat("\nNumeric Columns Summary:\n")
    for (col in names(x$numeric_summary)) {
      stats <- x$numeric_summary[[col]]
      cat(sprintf("\n  %s:\n", col))
      cat(sprintf("    Mean: %.2f, SD: %.2f\n", stats$mean, stats$sd))
      cat(sprintf("    Min: %.2f, Max: %.2f, Median: %.2f\n", 
                 stats$min, stats$max, stats$median))
      cat(sprintf("    Missing: %d (%.1f%%)\n", stats$missing, stats$missing_pct))
    }
  }
  
  if (length(x$categorical_summary) > 0) {
    cat("\nCategorical Columns Summary:\n")
    for (col in names(x$categorical_summary)) {
      stats <- x$categorical_summary[[col]]
      cat(sprintf("\n  %s:\n", col))
      cat(sprintf("    Unique values: %d\n", stats$n_unique))
      if (length(stats$top_categories) > 0) {
        cat(sprintf("    Top categories: %s\n", 
                   paste(stats$top_categories, collapse = ", ")))
      }
    }
  }
  
  cat("\n=== End Summary ===\n")
}
```



```{r}

library(DataTrans)
library(DataTrans)


boxcox_transform(c(1, 10, 100), lambda = 0.5)
log_transform(c(1, 10, 100))
minmax_normalization(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
```

```{r}
library(DataTrans)
library(readxl)

# Load necessary libraries
library(DataTrans)
library(readxl)

# Import the dataset
turbine_data <- read_excel("turbine_thrust.XLS", sheet = "Sheet1")
View(turbine_data)

# Inspect the dataset
print("Dataset Summary:")
print(summary(turbine_data))

print("Dataset Head:")
print(head(turbine_data))

# Check column names
print("Column Names:")
print(names(turbine_data))

# Replace "y" with your actual numeric column name if different
numeric_column_name <- "y"

if (!numeric_column_name %in% names(turbine_data)) {
    stop(paste("Column", numeric_column_name, "not found in the dataset."))
}

numeric_column <- turbine_data[[numeric_column_name]]

# Ensure no missing values (optional)
numeric_column <- na.omit(numeric_column)

# Check if values are positive (for Box-Cox and Log transformations)
print(paste("Minimum value in", numeric_column_name, ":", min(numeric_column)))
print(paste("Maximum value in", numeric_column_name, ":", max(numeric_column)))

# 1. Box-Cox Transformation
print("Applying Box-Cox Transformation...")

tryCatch({
    boxcox_result <- boxcox_transform(numeric_column)
    print(head(boxcox_result))
}, error = function(e) print(paste("Error in Box-Cox Transformation:", e)))

# 2. Log Transformation
print("Applying Log Transformation...")

tryCatch({
    log_result <- log_transform(numeric_column)
    print(head(log_result))
}, error = function(e) print(paste("Error in Log Transformation:", e)))

# 3. Min-Max Normalization
print("Applying Min-Max Normalization...")

tryCatch({
    minmax_result <- minmax_normalization(numeric_column)
    print(head(minmax_result))
}, error = function(e) print(paste("Error in Min-Max Normalization:", e)))

# 4. Moving Average
print("Calculating Moving Average...")

tryCatch({
    # Check function signature - might be different parameter name
    moving_avg_result <- moving_average(numeric_column, window_size = 5)
    print(head(moving_avg_result))
}, error = function(e) {
    print(paste("Error in Moving Average:", e))
    # Try alternative parameter name
    tryCatch({
        moving_avg_result <- moving_average(numeric_column, n = 5)
        print(head(moving_avg_result))
    }, error = function(e2) print(paste("Alternative also failed:", e2)))
})

# If you want to try other transformations from the package:
print("Available functions in DataTrans package:")
print(ls("package:DataTrans"))

# Additional transformations you might want to try:

# 5. Polynomial Transform
print("Applying Polynomial Transform...")
tryCatch({
    poly_result <- polynomial_transform(numeric_column, degree = 2)
    print(head(poly_result))
}, error = function(e) print(paste("Error in Polynomial Transform:", e)))

# 6. Score Transform
print("Applying Score Transform...")
tryCatch({
    score_result <- score_transform(numeric_column)
    print(head(score_result))
}, error = function(e) print(paste("Error in Score Transform:", e)))
```
